brief: GS forecasts September core CPI +0.24% m/m (vs +0.2% consensus, +2.46% y/y vs +2.5%) and headline CPI +0.59% (vs +0.6%), consistent with a slightly smaller 0.20% core PCE rise. In GOAL, GS shifts to OW Equities and UW Credit over 3m and OW Bonds (12m) plus tactical OW Cash, arguing earnings growth plus the recent valuation de-rating improves asymmetry into Q3 earnings; it sees long-duration bonds gaining medium-term value as inflation normalises and the Fed turns less hawkish, but still prefers shorter-duration cash tactically now. Europe industrials inventory check: China above-normal but falling, Europe elevated, US lean except Machinery/Automotive; electrical equipment is most depleted (all-time lows), depletion spread across Metals, Machinery, Hardware, Manufacturing, Computer Equipment, Chemicals. LVMH's 3Q cFX sales grew 1% in line, but Fashion & Leather fell -5% cFX, worse than already-lowered expectations, driven by a China-led mid-teens slowdown. GS initiates CTS Eventim Neutral (EUR68 PT) after a ~50% de-rating on competition/capital-allocation concerns. Orsted is cut to Neutral on rates up 50-65bp since August (+100bp YTD), weak Q3 expected, new DKK155 PT only 15% upside. Zurich Insurance reinstated Neutral: attractive EPS growth ex-Beazley plus Beazley uplift, but valuation has compressed near peers.
